subject: ADR-017's Flex Pitch modules and their reachability
question: Can any operation reach the Flex Pitch modules, so note identity could be exercised at all?

host.note: about the SERVER binary's wiring, not Logic; host recorded so drift is still dated

reverify.command: grep -rn FlexPitch Sources/ --include=*.swift | grep -v '^Sources/LogicProMCP/FlexPitch/' and check who reads FeatureFlags.adr017FlexPitch.
reverify.expected: the only hit outside the module directory is the flag's own declaration, and the only reader is a test asserting the flag is off

method: Searched every reference to FlexPitch outside its own directory, and every reader of the ADR-017 feature flag, across Sources and Tests. This measures REACHABILITY, which is the precondition for any note-identity measurement: a surface no operation can enter cannot have its identity stability exercised.
conclusion: The Flex Pitch modules are pure logic with no caller. Nothing outside their own directory references them, the feature flag defaults off, and its only reader is a test asserting it is off. So the note-identity-stability measurement this ADR needs cannot be made through the product — there is no path that produces a FlexPitchSnapshot from a live region. This is the same shape as ADR-015: the modules exist and the live ingestion boundary in front of them does not.
limits: This measures reachability in the code, not Logic's Audio Track Editor. Whether Logic exposes stable note identity there is still unmeasured and is the ADR's actual question.
A walk of the Audio Track Editor's AX tree over a Flex-analysed region would answer that independently of wiring, and needs an audio region with Flex Pitch analysis — this project has none.
Says nothing about whether the modules' logic is correct; only that nothing calls it.
